[MUQATIL:20:48-53/r4] MUQATIL, d. 150 · مؤمن آل فرعون | reports | A believer from Pharaoh's family warned of destruction like that of Noah, Ad, Thamud, and later peoples, prompting Pharaoh to ask about earlier generations. | mentions 40:30, 40:31
[MUQATIL:20:48-53/r5] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | Moses could not tell Pharaoh the fate of earlier generations because the Torah was revealed only after Pharaoh and his people were destroyed.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتبيانأملمدخلتعلىحروفالاستفهامولمتدخلعلىالألف)#520/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | أم may precede من and هل, but not interrogative alif, because أم is itself equivalent to the alif particle.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتبيانأملمدخلتعلىحروفالاستفهامولمتدخلعلىالألف)#520/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Interrogative أسماء such as أي, من, ما, and متى do not need alif: the question is already marked and the alif is omitted as redundant.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتبيانأملمدخلتعلىحروفالاستفهامولمتدخلعلىالألف)#520/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | أم is needed to mark a shift from one alternative to another, while interrogative alif only initiates a question and is therefore omitted when redundant.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرالأسماءالمبهمة)#631/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Demonstratives keep their ordinary initial vowels in the diminutive, unlike other nouns, and add final alifs to distinguish their endings.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرالأسماءالمبهمة)#631/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Examples include هذا to هذيا, ذاك to ذياك, and ألا to أليا; the added alif gives them distinctive endings.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرالأسماءالمبهمة)#631/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The diminutive yāʾ in ذا is underlyingly third; one yāʾ is deleted when the sounds accumulate, and تيا is the diminutive of تا.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرالأسماءالمبهمة)#631/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The forms تماني and هاتا occur in poetry; Sibawayh cites Kaʿb al-Ghanawī and ʿImrān ibn Ḥiṭṭān.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرالأسماءالمبهمة)#631/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Elongated أولاء becomes ألياء; feminine forms avoid the same diminutive pattern when it could cause confusion.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرالأسماءالمبهمة)#631/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The relative pronouns الذي and التي take diminutive forms اللذيا and اللتيا, supported by al-ʿAjjāj's line.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرالأسماءالمبهمة)#631/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The final alifs disappear in dual forms through frequent use; the text gives corresponding singular, plural, and dual forms for demonstratives and relatives.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرالأسماءالمبهمة)#631/r8] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | من and أي are not diminished when used as relative pronouns because they remain interrogative forms, while الذي is treated like a demonstrative.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرالأسماءالمبهمة)#631/r9] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | اللاتي has no diminutive because اللتيات, the plural of اللتيا, supplies the needed form; Sibawayh compares this to using مسيان and عشيان instead of a diminutive of قصر.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرالمؤنث)#629/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The diminutive of a three-letter feminine noun adds tāʾ to distinguish it from the masculine form.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرالمؤنث)#629/r10] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Sibawayh leaves the diminutive of a man's name عين or أذن without tāʾ; Yūnus adds tāʾ and cites أذينة, itself a diminutive name.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرالمؤنث)#629/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الخليل | reports | Al-Khalil says tāʾ was added to mark femininity, but ʿanāq omits it because its length makes the extra marker heavy.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرالمؤنث)#629/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A longer feminine such as samāʾ is shortened in the diminutive and then behaves like a three-letter noun, giving سميّة.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرالمؤنث)#629/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A woman named Siqāʾ takes سقيقي without a feminine suffix because the proper name is already complete.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرالمؤنث)#629/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Sibawayh reports two diminutive analyses for ḥubārā: حبيرة preserves a feminine marker, while the other leaves the remaining form as four letters.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرالمؤنث)#629/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A feminine word with the feminine alif in fifth position or later takes the diminutive pattern shown by لغيزى to لغيغيزة.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرالمؤنث)#629/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Half, when used as an adjective of a woman, remains masculine in the diminutive because it is a masculine adjective shared with feminine nouns; the same applies to رضى and خليق.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرالمؤنث)#629/r8] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Sibawayh reports al-Khalil's account of the she-camel word الناب as masculine in the diminutive, نييب, because the masculine name became its established designation.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرالمؤنث)#629/r9] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A woman named حجر takes feminine حجيرة because حجر is a pure proper name, not a shared masculine adjective; a woman named فرس similarly takes فريسة.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهألفالتأنيثبعدألففمنعهذلكمنالانصراففي#530/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Feminine forms ending in two alifs, with the second represented by hamza, are diptote in both definite and indefinite use.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهألفالتأنيثبعدألففمنعهذلكمنالانصراففي#530/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The hamza is a substitute for the second alif to avoid two adjacent vowelless letters, and behaves like the alif it replaces.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهألفالتأنيثبعدألففمنعهذلكمنالانصراففي#530/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The feminine double alif is never added merely to lengthen a triliteral noun; the pattern is reserved for feminine marking.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهألفالتأنيثبعدألففمنعهذلكمنالانصراففي#530/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In ʿalbāʾ and ḥirbāʾ the hamza replaces yāʾ, and alif plus yāʾ lengthens triliteral nouns; these are distinct from the feminine double-alif pattern.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهألفالتأنيثبعدألففمنعهذلكمنالانصراففي#530/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Some Arabs say قوباء as a masculine declinable form, assimilating it to فسطاط; its masculine use and declension support that analysis.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهألفالتأنيثبعدألففمنعهذلكمنالانصراففي#530/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Ghawghāʾ has two analyses: feminine like ʿawrāʾ and diptote, or masculine and declinable like qaḍqāḍ because its sounds are reduplicated.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايلزمالواوفيهبدلالياء)#794/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الخليل | reports | For verbs of five or more letters, forms such as أغزيت and غازيت use yāʾ for wāw: the imperfect loses wāw under kasra and has already shifted to yāʾ.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايلزمالواوفيهبدلالياء)#794/r10] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | قيقاء and زيزاء follow علباء, since a form like قلقال occurs only as a verbal noun.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايلزمالواوفيهبدلالياء)#794/r11] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | An added yāʾ in fourth position behaves like a root consonant, so سلقيت and جعبيت follow ضوضيت and قوقيت.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايلزمالواوفيهبدلالياء)#794/r12] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | المروراة follows الشجوجاة and صمحمح, rather than عثوثل, because the صمحمح pattern is more common.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايلزمالواوفيهبدلالياء)#794/r13] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | قيقاءة and زيزاءة are singular forms of قيقاء and زيزاء; some also say قيقاءة وقواق, treating yāʾ as a substitute as in قيل.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايلزمالواوفيهبدلالياء)#794/r14] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | أثفية is فعليّة for speakers who say أثفت, but أفعولة for those who say ثفيت.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايلزمالواوفيهبدلالياء)#794/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الخليل | reports | In تغازينا and ترجينا, alif substitutes for the yāʾ that replaced wāw; the tāʾ is added to غازيت and رجيت.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايلزمالواوفيهبدلالياء)#794/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In ضوضيت and قوقيت, reduplicating a pair works like repeating one consonant: the doubled wāws parallel the doubled yāʾ of حييت and wāws of قوة.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايلزمالواوفيهبدلالياء)#794/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Forms such as حاحيت and عاعيت likewise repeat two consonants; alif is substituted for yāʾ because of their resemblance, as forms like الحيحاء and العيعاء show.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايلزمالواوفيهبدلالياء)#794/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الخليل | reports | دهديت الجعل is analyzed as دهدهت: yāʾ replaces hāʾ because the letters resemble one another in lightness and unobtrusiveness.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايلزمالواوفيهبدلالياء)#794/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | غوغاء has two analyses: feminine, uninflected like عوراء, or masculine and declinable, with doubled root consonants like قمقام.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايلزمالواوفيهبدلالياء)#794/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | On the masculine analysis, غوغاء is declinable like قمقام; other reduplicated forms are analogized to this type or to three-letter reduplication such as غصص and غصة.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايلزمالواوفيهبدلالياء)#794/r8] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In موماة, like دوداة and مرمر, the first mīm is part of the root; this common pattern is unlike تمسكن, since an extra initial mīm is rare here.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايلزمالواوفيهبدلالياء)#794/r9] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The alif in فيفاة is extra because الفيّف is also used with the same meaning.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكاضربأيهمهوأفضلواضربأيهمكانأفضلواضربأيهمأبوهزيد#444/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A relative clause after أيهم is acceptable when it contains هو; without هو, a form such as أيهم عاقل is judged awkward.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكاضربأيهمهوأفضلواضربأيهمكانأفضلواضربأيهمأبوهزيد#444/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Al-Khalil reports the rare construction ما أنا بالذي قائل لك شيئا from an Arab speaker.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكاضربأيهمهوأفضلواضربأيهمكانأفضلواضربأيهمأبوهزيد#444/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · autho
